items.a: Not "doing something a lot" — **persistent harmful use despite consequences**. Rats will self-stimulate to starvation; **persistence despite destruction** is the sine qua non.

items.q: Do genes decide who gets addicted?
items.a: Genes matter but **aren't destiny**. A parent's alcoholism history beats SNP panels; liking is substance-specific (Humphreys hates opioids; others feel a "hole filled").

items.q: Why does age of first use matter so much?
items.a: **Plasticity cuts both ways** — almost all addictions start in teens. Start smoking at **13** → almost certainly addicted; start at Humphreys's age → probably won't.

items.q: Is a little alcohol actually healthy?
items.a: **Zero is better than any** for alcohol. Cardiac benefit is outweighed by cancer risk; the J-curve myth comes from **sick quitters**. Even **2 drinks/week** = tiny but real excess risk.

items.q: Who is genetically at higher alcohol risk?
items.a: Schuckit's **low-punishment genotype** — less body sway, fewer hangovers → higher risk. The industry exploits this: **~10% of US drinkers consume ~50%** of alcohol.

items.q: Why isn't today's cannabis the same drug as the 1980s?
items.a: Potency jumped **3–5% → ~20% THC**; **42%** of users are daily. A 15-year-old on modern weed ≈ vodka vs a parent's low-alcohol beer — ~**65× brain exposure** vs 1980s weekend use.

items.q: How do addiction industries engineer use?
items.a: **More addiction is good for your bottom line.** Slots optimize **novelty and losses disguised as wins**; apps ask how to make themselves more addictive.

items.q: What is the only sure way a substance won't damage your life?
items.a: Anna Lembke's line: **you can't get addicted to what you never use** — "the only way to determine that a substance will not damage your life is to **never use it** in the first place."

Cochrane: AA ~**50% better abstinence vs CBT** for alcohol — "the closest thing we have to a **free lunch in public health**." Not a cult (no money grab; leave anytime); higher power = **anything but you**.

items.q: How should you talk to someone with addiction?
items.a: Use **motivational interviewing** — ask why *they* want to quit; don't lecture. **91%** of alcohol-treatment seekers got external pressure before seeking help.

**GLP-1s** (semaglutide) can cut alcohol craving — patients "want **not to want**." Stimulants respond best to **contingency management** (escalating rewards for clean urines). SAINT TMS and carefully licensed psychedelics are emerging clinical tools.
